subject_definitions
<Subject 1> is the person defined by the character sheet in <Picture 1>. Use the sheet as the sole character reference, without adding a written description of the character's appearance or clothing.

summary
[reference generation] A ten-second photorealistic dessert-table micro-story. <Subject 1> secretly tastes a little cake, hears someone approach, and tries to look innocent. An off-screen friend points out the cream at the corner of her mouth. She checks it, realizes she has been caught, and breaks into an embarrassed, genuine laugh.

retention_analysis
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved from <Picture 1> across all shots.
<Picture 1> defines the character only, not a mandatory first frame, pose, environment, or layout. Do not reproduce sheet panels, repeated figures, labels, or reference backgrounds.
The friend remains off-screen except for one brief pointing hand. Introduce one small cream-covered cake on a white plate and one teaspoon as scene props.

detailed_description
Photorealistic cinematic imagery beside a softly lit café window, with natural skin texture, delicate lip detail, and a believable matte, whipped-cream texture. Use horizontal 16:9 composition, clear facial illumination, restrained warm colors, and natural real-time performance throughout.

[Shot 1] Begin with an eye-level medium close-up of <Subject 1> seated at a small dessert table. Include the face, hands, and plated cake. The teaspoon in her right hand already holds one small bite. She gives a quick sideways glance, then tastes it with a tiny, private smile. As the spoon leaves her lips, a small dab of white cream remains just beside the right corner of her mouth. Show this as a result of contact, not cream appearing from nowhere. She lowers the spoon onto the same plate and finishes the small bite naturally. Keep the plate supported on the table and avoid extra utensils.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.000, cut to a facial close-up from the same side of her eyeline. Two quiet approaching footsteps make her look up toward an unseen friend beside the camera. She closes her lips, straightens slightly, and carefully adopts an innocent expression as if she has not touched the cake. Her eyes remain a little too attentive, revealing the effort. Keep the same small cream mark at the right corner of her mouth, with the same position, size, and texture across the cut. Do not erase it or smear it over her whole cheek.

[Shot 3] At 00:05.000, cut to a slightly wider facial-and-upper-chest close-up, leaving space at one edge for a hand. One naturally connected hand from the off-screen friend briefly enters and points toward the cream, stopping short without touching her face. The hand withdraws. Her eyes follow the gesture; she hesitates, then uses her left index fingertip to lightly touch the marked corner of her own mouth. Keep her face visible during the gesture, with anatomically natural fingers and contact.

A little cream transfers onto her fingertip, leaving only a faint trace at the mouth. She looks down at the cream on her finger and immediately understands. Her controlled innocent expression falters: her brows lift slightly, her eyes soften, and she gives one short, sheepish laugh. She lowers the hand away from her face as the smile becomes spontaneous. The cream transfers through the touch, never disappearing between frames. Keep the reaction playful and understated, not cartoonish or flirtatiously exaggerated.

Let the camera make only a minimal, slow forward move during the last shot. End on her unguarded smile, with the original cake and spoon unchanged below the crop. Preserve the same identity and consistent soft light throughout. No dialogue, additional faces, duplicated hands, oversized cream splashes, plastic skin, oily facial highlights, slow motion, freeze frames, subtitles, or logos.

overall_soundscape
Quiet café room tone, a delicate spoon-to-plate contact near the end of Shot 1, two approaching footsteps at Shot 2, a faint clothing rustle with the pointing gesture, and one short natural laugh at the end. No intelligible speech or exaggerated chewing.

non_diegetic_music
N/A
